description: Competing in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Coimbatore), our team is analyzing microgravity combustion data with AI/ML to uncover critical fire safety insights for space missions, space stations, and Earth. We are looking for teammates skilled in AI/ML, web/app development, UI/UX design, and content/research—join us to build innovative space tech!
summary:
FIRELYTICS AI is an independent research workbench developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Flame in Freefall challenge. It brings NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion research and selected archived SAME-R analysis into one interactive platform for exploring spacecraft fire-safety evidence.

The platform deeply indexes 14 investigations from a wider repository scope of 24 studies and includes tools for comparing experiments, exploring hypothetical space-habitat conditions, and analysing six archived SAME-R experimental runs. Users can examine how oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, gravity and material conditions relate to combustion research.

FIRELYTICS addresses the challenge by making complex microgravity-combustion research easier to explore, compare and understand. It also highlights scientific assumptions, evidence gaps and the limitations of calculated results, helping researchers investigate fire-safety questions relevant to future crewed missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
About FIRELYTICS AI

FIRELYTICS AI is an interactive scientific research platform developed to make NASA microgravity combustion research easier to explore and understand. It connects NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigation metadata with selected archived SAME-R analysis to support research into spacecraft fire safety.

How the Project Works

The application provides five main research workspaces:

  1. Mission & Habitat Simulator: Allows users to explore five hypothetical research profiles, including ISS, lunar and Martian environments. Users can adjust oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, gravity and material inputs and examine the resulting screening calculations.
  2. Catalogue & Comparison Matrix: Organizes 14 deeply indexed NASA PSI investigations and allows users to compare experimental conditions, fuel phases, hardware and research parameters.
  3. SI Fire-Safety Synthesis: Organizes research around prevention, detection, suppression, partial-gravity conditions and potential applications on Earth.
  4. SAME-R Telemetry & Lineage Lab: Provides access to reconciled archived analysis from six selected PSI-101 Pyrell runs, including cycle classifications, validation checks and source-row references.
  5. All-in-One Executive View: Brings the major research workspaces together for a unified overview.

The application also includes scientific visualizations for oxygen-pressure conditions, partial-gravity screening, evidence ranking and SAME-R archive analysis.

Technology Used

The frontend is developed using Next.js, React and TypeScript. The backend uses Python and FastAPI, with Pydantic for request validation. A Next.js API proxy connects the browser to the backend. Scientific calculations, catalogue matching and reporting are handled by the backend, with results displayed through browser-native SVG and HTML/CSS visualizations.

The platform distinguishes NASA source metadata, archived analysis and code-generated screening outputs. Its ranking, evidence coverage and physics-proximity measures are presented separately rather than as fire-risk scores. Its partial-gravity and minimum-oxygen-concentration calculations are exploratory screening surrogates, not validated fire predictions.

Innovation and Intended Impact

The main strength of FIRELYTICS is bringing different combustion investigations into one traceable research environment. It helps users understand the available evidence, compare experimental conditions and identify gaps that require future research.

The project also explores potential research connections to smoke-versus-dust detection, fine-water-mist suppression and fire-resistant material screening.

By making scientific assumptions and limitations visible, FIRELYTICS aims to support better-informed fire-safety research for future human missions to the Moon and Mars.

Project Website: https://firelytics-ai.vercel.app/

Source Code: https://github.com/mantuchaurasiya092-source/firelytics-ai

For detailed information about the project's scientific methodology, system architecture, implementation, data processing, and technical design, refer to our technical documentation:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rkG3dfFZfJCMFG79XQFZlMp0PNZ-EdIl/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=116056661474776921869&rtpof=true&sd=true

FIRELYTICS AI is an independent educational and research prototype. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by NASA.
